reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its main activity is demonstrating how to install MetaMask, create a wallet, and transfer ETH from Coinbase to the wallet. The creator explicitly warns viewers not to disclose their seed phrase, and the description's Coinbase referral is presented as a conditional signup rebate rather than a promise of investment returns or a recruitment-dependent benefit.

citations.quote: hit install metamask for Chrome
you should never show this phrase to anyone
So just copy this and this is sending to Metamask.
don't forget to use the link down in the description box below
you and I both benefit and you get some rebates ($10 off your first $100)

opening.argument: The video links concrete viewer actions to financial and digital-asset benefits. It directs viewers to use the creator's Coinbase referral link, says both parties benefit, and advertises a $10 rebate after signing up and spending through the service. It then instructs viewers to install MetaMask, transfer ETH, and use the resulting balance to activate Ethereum businesses and platforms. That is a solicitation built around an easy wallet-and-signup pathway, not merely abstract education: the viewer is encouraged to register, move crypto, and expect a stated benefit.

citations.quote: use my referral link, https://coinbase.com/join/yan_nam you and I both benefit and you get some rebates ($10 off your first $100) when you sign up with me.
just hit on download install metamask for your browser
now you have Ethereum in your Metamask wallet that you can use to activate any Ethereum business and any Ethereum platform

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the mechanics but does not answer the solicitation. A tutorial can still function as a funnel when it pairs installation and crypto transfer with a referral reward. Calling the rebate conditional does not remove the promised benefit; the description expressly says the creator and viewer both benefit. Nor does a seed-phrase warning explain why viewers are directed toward the referral and crypto-activation pathway.

citations.quote: you and I both benefit and you get some rebates ($10 off your first $100)
that you can use to activate any Ethereum business and any Ethereum platform

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted rebate is a conventional, disclosed signup incentive, not a promise of investment income or a free asset: it requires signing up and is described as a rebate on a first purchase. The wallet instructions likewise show transfer of ETH to the viewer's own MetaMask address, while the video warns that the seed phrase must remain private. Those facts do not establish deceptive acquisition of funds.

citations.quote: you get some rebates ($10 off your first $100) when you sign up with me.
This is the Crypto address, or this is my Wallet address for people to send tokens to me
you should never show this phrase to anyone because it's like the password on your password

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: cryptocurrency transfers, an external referral link, a stated rebate, and language presenting Ethereum earnings and named crowdfunding businesses. The description says MetaMask is approved for automatically calculating earnings and identifies EzyEth and Forsage, while the tutorial moves viewers from an existing wallet into MetaMask and says the balance can activate Ethereum businesses. Even without an explicit guaranteed return, this combination makes the operational demonstration a persuasive route into financially risky participation.

citations.quote: approved for automatically calculating your earnings of ethereum on ethereum platforms and community crowdfunding businesses such as EzyEth, Forsage.
There is a very small network fee There is no Coinbase fee
it's on main ethereum network
use my referral link

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates the instructional steps and treats the warning as dispositive, but it does not address the surrounding earnings language, named crowdfunding platforms, referral link, or crypto movement. A process can be easy to follow precisely because it is designed to lower hesitation. The fact that the presenter does not reveal the seed phrase does not make the broader earnings-and-participation framing benign.

citations.quote: automatically calculating your earnings of ethereum
community crowdfunding businesses such as EzyEth, Forsage.
And I wanna send ETH

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals do not prove a scam category. The description calls the content a MetaMask tutorial and the recording demonstrates installation and a transfer, while the cited earnings sentence does not promise a fixed return, passive yield, or guaranteed profit. The referral is separately disclosed as a $10-off rebate, and the transfer uses a wallet address rather than sending money to the presenter.

citations.quote: Crypto Tutorial: Transfer Ethereum to METAMASK Wallet
today I want to show you how to download Metamask on your Chrome extension
you get some rebates ($10 off your first $100)
This long string of numbers is your Metamask address

opening.argument: Although presented as education, the video repeatedly steers viewers toward participation. It tells them where to obtain MetaMask, demonstrates moving ETH from Coinbase, directs them to the description's referral links, and closes by saying the resulting ETH can activate Ethereum businesses and platforms. The creator also promotes a Coinbase signup benefit in the description, where both parties allegedly benefit. The tutorial format therefore operates as promotional onboarding: explanation is used to normalize registration, funding, and continued use of crypto services.

citations.quote: just head over to Metamask.io or you can type in Metamask on Google
So just copy this and this is sending to Metamask.
don't forget to use the link down in the description box below
you and I both benefit and you get some rebates ($10 off your first $100)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense labels the format a demonstration, but that does not resolve its promotional effect. The creator does not merely explain wallet concepts: viewers are directed to MetaMask, shown how to send ETH, told to use the description link, and offered a mutual benefit. A tutorial can be the delivery mechanism for recruitment into a crypto service even when its steps are technically accurate.

citations.quote: just hit on download install metamask for your browser
I want to transfer it from Coinbase
you and I both benefit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The actions shown are ordinary wallet operations and are not evidence that viewers are recruited into a deceptive scheme. The content explicitly explains how to protect the recovery phrase and shows ETH being sent to the MetaMask address. The only stated incentive is a disclosed Coinbase rebate, not income dependent on recruiting others or a promise that transferred ETH will appreciate.
